item.title: Finnable Nets ₹405 Cr To Scale Digital Lending Business
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Bengaluru-based digital lending startup Finnable has raised ₹405 Cr ($43.8 Mn) in a Series C funding round led by Bharat…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based digital lending startup Finnable has raised ₹405 Cr ($43.8 Mn) in a Series C funding round led by Bharat Value Fund (BVF), which invested ₹150 Cr in the startup.

The round also saw participation from Pratithi Investments and NK Squared, along with existing investors TVS Capital and MEMG Family Office.

Finnable will deploy the fresh capital to expand its lending portfolio, strengthen its tech stack and forge new partnerships across the lending ecosystem.

Founded in 2015 by Nitin Gupta, Viraj Tyagi and Amit Arora, Finnable is a personal loan platform offering quick, paperless loans ranging from ₹25,000 to ₹10 Lakh. It primarily serves mid-income salaried professionals earning between ₹15,000-50,000 per month.

Finnable has scaled its lending operations significantly, with its consolidated assets under management (AUM) stood at over ₹4,600 Cr as of this October.

The startup also reported a profit after tax (PAT) of ₹51 Cr in the first half of FY27, surpassing the ₹46 Cr profit it recorded for the entire FY26. The startup didn’t disclose its top line performance for the period.

The bottom line growth came at the behest of  expansion beyond personal lending. The NBFC began offering loans against property in June 2025, although the product remains at a relatively early stage.

The latest fundraise comes a year after Finnable announced a ₹500 Cr equity raise led by Z47 and TVS Capital. Prior to that, the company raised ₹30.5 Cr in a Series B round.

India’s Digital Lending Opportunity

Finnable’s latest fundraise comes amid continued investor interest in India’s retail credit and digital lending market, particularly as lenders look to serve borrowers who remain underserved by traditional banking channels

To note, around 8 Cr aspirational borrowers accounted for 79% of India’s 14 Cr retail credit originations between January and March 2026, according to Equifax India’s recent report. These borrowers represented ₹19 Lakh Cr of the total ₹24 Lakh Cr in retail credit originations during the period.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also reported a 22% YoY increase in NBFC retail lending in August, compared with 13.6% growth a year earlier, Finnable said.

With India’s fintech sector projected to reach $250 Bn in revenue by 2030, lending tech startups are expected to contribute over 53% of that growth.

Electronics design and manufacturing startup Elecbits is in talks to raise fresh capital in the range of $12-15 Mn in a fresh funding round led by PE firm Xponentia Capital, sources familiar with the development told Inc42.

Existing investors, including Nexus Venture Partners, are also likely to participate in the round.

Inc42 reached out to Elecbits and Xponentia Capital for comments on the proposed fundraise. However, neither responded to queries at the time of publishing this story. The capital to be raised is yet to be finalised.

Founded in 2019 by Saurav Kumar Singh and Nikhil Rawat, Elecbits operates a full-stack electronics design and manufacturing platform, helping businesses take hardware products from concept and prototyping to manufacturing and delivery.

The startup offers services across the electronics manufacturing value chain, including printed circuit board (PCB) design, firmware development, component sourcing, PCB fabrication and assembly, quality control and final product manufacturing.

It also operates Elecbits XOR, an AI-powered electronics engineering and manufacturing platform that offers instant quotations, component intelligence, supply chain visibility and risk management tools.

The platform aims to simplify the traditionally fragmented electronics manufacturing ecosystem by bringing engineering, procurement and manufacturing workflows under one roof.

Elecbits caters to businesses across digital payments, power electronics, IT hardware, automotive and consumer electronics. It claims to work with over 200 companies, including Panasonic, Schneider Electric, Motherson, Maruti Suzuki, Urban Company, Zetwerk and Ola Electric.

The startup positions itself as a vertically integrated manufacturing partner for companies looking to diversify their supply chains beyond China under the China+1 strategy.

In December 2025, Elecbits raised $5.5 Mn in a Series A funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners. The round also saw participation from SE Ventures and Riverwalk Holdings.

The fresh fundraise comes amid growing investments in India’s electronics manufacturing ecosystem, supported by government initiatives such as the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme and the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS).

As India looks to deepen its domestic electronics manufacturing capabilities and reduce reliance on imports, startups building design, engineering and component supply chain capabilities are looking to capitalise on the opportunity.

For Elecbits, the proposed $15 Mn round could provide additional capital to expand its manufacturing capabilities, strengthen its technology platform and scale its enterprise business.

item.title: SC Orders Separate Warning Labels For High Fat, Sugar, And Salt In Packaged Foods
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Supreme Court has reportedly directed the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to ensure…
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court has reportedly directed the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to ensure that packaged foods carry separate pictorial warning labels for high levels of fat, sugar and salt.

A bench comprising Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said each warning under the front-of-package nutrition labelling (FOPNL) framework must include a standard pictorial representation of the nutrient of concern, alongside the corresponding words “HIGH FAT”, “HIGH SUGAR” or “HIGH SALT”.

According to a Live Law report, products exceeding prescribed thresholds for more than one nutrient must carry separate hexagonal warnings for each, rather than a single combined label.

The direction tightens FSSAI’s proposal, which provided for the relevant nutrients to be identified within one hexagon.

The court also directed the government to ensure strict implementation of existing regulations, including the 2020 rules.

The SC also asked the Centre to strengthen nutritional literacy among children by introducing changes in school curricula, introducing interactive workshops as well co-curricular activities in school.

From Ratings To Warnings

FSSAI initially proposed a health-star rating system in 2022, but the plan did not translate into a mandatory labelling regime. Its approach subsequently shifted towards red hexagonal warnings for packaged foods exceeding prescribed nutrient thresholds.

The regulator initially proposed a two-phase rollout, covering products high in two or more specified nutrients before extending warnings to those high in any one nutrient. The petitioner challenged the two-nutrient threshold as scientifically unjustified.

The SC also sought clarity on added versus total sugar and fat, the treatment of trans fats and sweetened beverages, and whether ultra-processed foods should face the same thresholds as other packaged foods.

FSSAI’s revised proposal provides for warnings when any one specified nutrient exceeds thresholds drawn from the Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024, issued by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition, irrespective of the degree of food processing.

It also envisages a separate warning for products containing non-caloric sweeteners, reading “CONTAIN NON CALORIC SWEETENER”.

Before the verdict, FSSAI had sought approximately four months to issue and finalise the draft regulations through the prescribed regulatory process. It had also proposed a 365-day voluntary implementation period after notification.

Implications For D2C Brands

The directions have particular significance for D2C food brands that have built their positioning around healthier ingredients and clean-label claims.

Front-of-pack warnings could require brands to revisit formulations, packaging, and marketing. Alternative ingredients, taste trials, laboratory testing, and shelf-life adjustments could increase costs, particularly for smaller companies.

The scrutiny predates today’s verdict. In September, Inc42 reported that at least 20 new-age D2C food brands had received FSSAI notices since May over claims involving added sugar, natural ingredients, and organic positioning.

Some brands have already changed their packaging language post the clamp down. MasterChow dropped “100% Natural” from its ramen packaging, while Pluckk told Inc42 it would add “contains naturally occurring sugar” alongside its “no added sugar” claim.

The regulator is also examining disclosures on their distribution channels. FSSAI is considering dedicated rules for ecommerce platforms, quick commerce companies, and cloud kitchens.

The proposed requirements include displaying manufacturing and expiry dates and batch numbers on online listings, greater platform accountability for misleading manufacturer claims, and disclosure of cloud kitchen photographs and addresses.

item.title: WhatsApp Rolls Out Message Scheduling Up To 14 Days In Advance
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Meta-owned WhatsApp has introduced scheduled messages, allowing users to draft texts, photos, and videos for delivery at a later date…
item.content:encoded:
Meta-owned WhatsApp has introduced scheduled messages, allowing users to draft texts, photos, and videos for delivery at a later date and time.

Users can schedule messages between 10 minutes and 14 days in advance across individual and group chats. The feature is rolling out globally over the coming weeks, the company said in a blog post.

WhatsApp global head Kunal Shah highlighted the launch in a post on X, saying, “Be the first one to wish for their birthdays now. Scheduled messages on WA now.”

WhatsApp described scheduled messaging as “one of our most requested features”, allowing users to prepare messages without having to remember to send them later.

To schedule a message, users need to compose it, press and hold the send button, and select a delivery date and time. Recipients will see it like any regular message, without an indication that it was scheduled.

Users can view their queued messages and delete them before delivery. WhatsApp said scheduled messages will arrive even if the sender’s phone is switched off or out of battery.

From Messaging To Everyday Services

The launch comes as WhatsApp looks to expand its utility beyond messaging under Shah, who took over as the platform’s global head earlier this year after stepping away from day-to-day operations at CRED.

Earlier this month, Shah outlined three broad priorities for WhatsApp — making communication more expressive, simplifying everyday services and integrating AI into the platform. The company is looking to make activities such as bill payments, financial transactions and accessing services easier to complete within WhatsApp.

In India, where WhatsApp has more than 500 Mn users, the company has also expanded its payments offering. In September, it launched in-app bill payments covering 22,722 billers across 30 categories, including electricity, gas, water, FASTag, insurance, and loan repayments.

The messaging platform has also expanded its payments offering in India. In September, WhatsApp launched in-app bill payments covering 22,722 billers across 30 categories, including electricity, gas, water, FASTag, insurance and loan repayments. The feature is powered by Bharat Connect and supports UPI, debit cards and credit cards.

item.title: XEBO.ai Bags $10.5 Mn To Expand Its Customer Experience Platform
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Dubai-headquartered experience management company XEBO.ai has raised $10.5 Mn (around ₹97.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round from Emirates…
item.content:encoded:
Dubai-headquartered experience management company XEBO.ai has raised $10.5 Mn (around ₹97.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round from Emirates Growth Fund (EGF), the UAE’s flagship growth equity investor.

EGF is the sole investor in the round, although the startup is in discussions with other investors who could join in the coming months, cofounder and CEO Yash Sultania told Inc42.

XEBO.ai will allocate 30-40% of the proceeds for product development to expand its voice-of-customer (VoC) offerings through voice analytics, digital analytics and agentic AI capabilities.

Around 30% of the capital will go towards strengthening its presence in existing markets, including the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), Africa, Asia Pacific and India. The remainder will fund its expansion into new geographies, with North America a key focus.

“We are a product company, and around 30-40% of the investment will go towards product development. We want to add more products to our portfolio, particularly around voice analytics, digital analytics and agentic AI,” Sultania said.

The startup also plans to step up its go-to-market efforts across existing markets while building its presence in North America. Cofounder Anand Nigam has relocated to the US to lead the expansion.

Founded in 2017, XEBO.ai operates an experience management platform that helps enterprises collect and analyse feedback. Its offerings span customer experience, employee experience, market research, social listening and customer journey mapping.

The startup was previously known as Survey2Connect before rebranding to XEBO.ai in late 2023. Its products help enterprises collect and analyse customer and employee feedback through surveys, voice-of-customer (VoC) analytics, customer journey mapping and social listening tools.

XEBO.ai said it serves more than 350 enterprises across over 10 industries, including banking, aviation, telecommunications, insurance, retail, healthcare and the public sector. Its clientele includes HSBC Middle East, Emirates Airlines, Starbucks, H&M, Dubai Properties and the Abu Dhabi government. In India, its clients include Tata AIG, Mahindra Group and others.

Around 200 of its clients are based in the Middle East, while more than 50 are in Europe and North America. The remaining clients are spread across Africa, India and Singapore, Sultania said. The startup has also integrated its platform with enterprise and digital experience tools such as Salesforce, enabling businesses to consolidate customer feedback from multiple channels.

XEBO.ai follows an annual subscription model, with contracts starting at $10,000 and going up to $200,000, depending on enterprise requirements. It competes with global experience management platforms such as Qualtrics and Medallia.

The startup employs more than 100 people, around 80% of whom are based in India. Its Indian operations, which include an office in Noida, are largely focused on product development and engineering.

While XEBO.ai has built much of its business in the Middle East, it plans to strengthen its go-to-market (GTM) operations in India. The startup is also looking to expand its presence in North America, with cofounder Anand Nigam relocating to the US to lead the expansion.

“We are looking to reach $100 Mn in ARR over the next four to five years. We are targeting accelerated growth in 2027 and 2028, and may raise another round of funding, potentially a Series B, in the next two years to support that growth,” Sultania told Inc42.

item.content:encoded:
Uber has appointed former Zomato food delivery CEO Rakesh Ranjan as its president for India and South Asia, as the ride-hailing platform looks to strengthen its presence in one of its largest global markets.

Ranjan will assume the role on January 4, 2027, and report to Dom Taylor, Uber’s regional general manager for Asia Pacific.

He will join Uber from edtech platform Allen Online, where he is currently the CEO. Prior to that, Ranjan spent eight years at Zomato, joining the foodtech company in 2017. During his stint, the ISB alumnus held leadership positions across Zomato Gold and sales before taking charge as CEO of its B2B offering Hyperpure, and eventually the food ordering and delivery business.

The appointment follows a search process spanning more than three months, according to Uber. Former president Prabhjet Singh, who held the post for 11 years, left Uber India in July to join OpenAI as its India MD. 

Commenting on the appointment, Taylor said Ranjan’s experience in running large consumer businesses in India and his understanding of the market made him a suitable fit to lead the company’s next phase of growth in the region.

Uber’s India Growth Ambitions

India is Uber’s third-largest market globally by trips, behind the US and Brazil, and its second-largest market by number of earners.

The company operates in more than 225 cities in India, with over two million monthly active drivers earning through its platform. India is also home to Uber’s largest technology centres outside the US, located in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, the company said. It is also setting up its first data centre in India in partnership with the Adani Group. 

Uber entered India in 2013 and has since expanded its mobility offerings beyond cabs to include bikes, autos and metro services.

Ranjan’s appointment comes as Uber looks to build on this scale by improving ride reliability, expanding value-oriented mobility options, and creating better earning opportunities for drivers.

In a statement, Ranjan said his priorities would include improving everyday customer experiences through dependable rides, offering value across different journeys and creating better earning opportunities for drivers.

India is expected to contribute a significant share of Uber’s global growth, the company said. Earlier this year, Uber infused ₹2,921 Cr into its India arm, as competition intensified in the country’s ride-hailing market, especially from Rapido, which is currently its biggest competitor.

Uber also undertook internal restructuring earlier this year, which saw the company lay off around 200-250 employees in India in September as part of a global layoff exercise that culled 3,300 roles across functions. The layoffs, which impacted both individual contributors and managers, came barely six months after Uber cut around 80 jobs in the country.

Despite healthy demand, Uber has been facing issues at multiple fronts in emerging markets like India and Brazil, including a mismatch in driver supply and elevated fuel prices. Since these are price sensitive markets, Uber is rejigging driver and rider incentives to retain supply, the company said during its Q4 2026 earnings call this month.

item.title: Green Aero Raises $14 Mn To Build Jet Engines, Combat Drones
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma

item.content:encoded:
Deeptech startup Green Aero has raised $14 Mn (₹129.2 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by Crane Ventures, as it looks to scale indigenous jet engine development and build autonomous combat aircraft for India and global markets.

The round also saw participation from 3one4 Capital, Antler Elevate, and existing investors pi Ventures, Antler India, and Rebalance. 

Founded in 2023 by Prithwish Kundu, Green Aero is developing jet propulsion systems, avionics and airframes for high-speed drones and autonomous combat aircraft. 

It will deploy the capital over the next 12-18 months to expand its engine testing infrastructure, hire engineers, develop larger-thrust engines and accelerate flight qualification of its transonic and supersonic drone platforms.

The startup is also looking to commercialise its existing engines, having received early interest from domestic and international buyers, Kundu told Inc42. 

The startup is building a vertically integrated aerospace manufacturing stack, bringing jet engines, avionics and airframe development under one roof. The company operates 87,000 sq ft R&D, assembly and testing facility in Bengaluru.

Kundu told Inc42 that the startup has completed more than 100 ground-fire tests and is now moving towards flight testing. The startup expects its flight-testing programme to continue over the next year, following which its larger-thrust engines and transonic drone platforms could move towards commercial deployment.

“The startup currently generates revenue through the supply of small engines, while larger engine categories are undergoing further testing,” Kundu added.

Green Aero has also developed its Blue Dragon engine core, which it claims is the first globally to demonstrate air-blast atomisers in the sub-kilonewton engine category. These atomisers are a form of fuel-injection technology generally used in larger jet engines.

The startup said its engines can operate on diesel as well as jet fuel, allowing them to cater to different applications across military drones and aerospace platforms.

Green Aero is now looking to develop engines in the four-kilonewton-plus category over the next three years, Kundu told Inc42. These larger engines are expected to power aircraft and drones capable of operating in the supersonic regime.

The startup is developing transonic drones powered by its existing sub-kilonewton engines, while its longer-term focus is on Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCAs), autonomous aircraft designed to operate alongside manned fighter jets or independently.

Kundu said the company is betting on the evolution of drone warfare towards faster, jet-powered and autonomous systems. 

The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in India’s propulsion technology ecosystem, spanning missile engines, aircraft propulsion and satellite systems. D-Propulse, which is developing rotating detonation engines for high-speed drones and missiles, raised ₹25 Cr from IAN Alpha Fund earlier this year and is working towards flight-ready propulsion systems. 

The startup has also demonstrated a 5 kN air-breathing rotating detonation engine and plans flight tests in 2027.

Meanwhile, Bellatrix Aerospace recently secured a multi-year contract from GalaxEye to supply propulsion systems for 30 satellites. 

On the other hand, Manastu Space has raised ₹22 Cr in an ongoing funding round to develop satellite propulsion and debris-avoidance technology.

While these startups are working across different propulsion applications, the growing funding and commercial contracts point to an emerging domestic ecosystem attempting to build critical aerospace hardware locally, reducing reliance on overseas suppliers.
